newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-UK GOVERNMENT SETS UP TASKFORCE FOR FANS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UK GOVERNMENT SETS UP TASKFORCE FOR FANS.

text.p: Britain's new Labour government on Wednesday established a taskforce to ensure a fair deal for English soccer fans, headed by David Mellor, a former minister in the Conservative government.
The taskforce will deal with issues that have increasingly affected the sport's reputation over recent years, Sports Minister Tony Banks said.
These included high ticket prices, hooliganism, racism and ever-increasing commercialisation.
Banks told a news conference it was "essential for football to think afresh about the safety and comfort of the spectators coming to watch our national game".

Mellor, like Banks and former prime minister John Major a fan of premier league Chelsea, expressed his delight at his appointment. The taskforce is expected to report back to the government by the end of the year.
He said he was committed to putting soccer back in the hands of the ordinary fan and would be "looking at the conflicts that arise when clubs go on to the stock market".

Mellor resigned as the minister in charge of arts and sports in 1992 after a much-publicised affair with an actress and allegations over accepting a free holiday. He lost his parliamentary seat at the May 1 election won by Labour.
